title: FutureFill: Fast Generation from Convolutional Sequence Models
claim: Our method keeps per-token generation cost constant as length grows, while baselines slow down and total time grows superlinearly.
layout: 2 side-by-side line plots, shared x-axis, total vs per-step
description: Two side-by-side line charts share the same x-axis, generation length L, which runs from 0 to 1e6. The left panel is titled 'Total generation time'. Its y-axis is S(L), in seconds. It shows total time growing for three methods. Blue Naive curves up steeply to about 200, with a shaded band for variance. Green Epoched-FutureFill grows more slowly to about 130. Red Continuous-FutureFill grows almost linearly to about 47. The right panel is titled 'Time per step', with S(L)/L on the y-axis. Blue Naive rises steadily to about 0.0002. Green rises to about 0.00013. Red stays flat at about 0.000045. The three curves cross near L=0.2e6. A large legend sits in the upper left of each panel. Thick saturated lines on a light grid draw the eye to the diverging curves.
caption: Total and average number of seconds per step when generating $L$ tokens, as a function of $L$.
abstract: We address the challenge of efficient auto-regressive generation in sequence prediction models by introducing FutureFill, a general-purpose fast generation method for any sequence prediction algorithm based on convolutional operators. FutureFill reduces generation time from quadratic to quasilinear in the context length. Moreover, when generating from a prompt, it requires a prefill cache whose size grows only with the number of tokens to be generated, often much smaller than the caches required by standard convolutional or attention based models. We validate our theoretical claims with experiments on synthetic tasks and demonstrate substantial efficiency gains when generating from a deep convolutional sequence prediction model.
